design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of prepaid_maintenance_plans, frozen 2026-10-21 10:15:00 EDT. Revision 2 (after policy audit revision_1).

1. Draw. `draw_counts.py ... --task 1` printed {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4]}. Root maintenance_ext_retail_plan_price = 4 factors; maintenance_ext_retail_cancel_refund = 4.

2. Why this is a good test. Celeste Marchetti asks only to buy a Kessler Care Plus 8-Visit plan for the Highlander delivered on 2026-10-07 at Kessler Toyota of Dayton. The purchase is a replacement purchase: her RAV4 (sold, no longer registered to her) carries Plus 8-Visit plan KC-305118 (sold on the RAV4's 2023 deal at 664.05, financed with Toyota Financial Services) with a signed cancellation request (vehicle_sold_or_traded, dated 2026-10-21, submitted). The retail price rule states "The retail plan price is fixed only after every Kessler Care Essentials, Plus or Premium plan of the customer that carries a signed cancellation request for a vehicle sold or traded stands cancelled." The agent must process that cancellation with its own four-factor refund (421.05), then price the replacement plan (269.50) and hand the contract to the customer.

3. Scope. Task 0 holds the fleet line (four policies, four tools). Task 1 claims maintenance_ext_retail_plan_price (user tool sign_care_plan_contract_c0d53aa0) and maintenance_ext_retail_cancel_refund (process_care_plan_cancellation_e800fe25). Disjoint; together all six policies are covered. The price computation's holding is the replaced plan KC-305118, which the rule names uniquely (the retail plan named on the customer's most recent signed sold-or-traded request; a tie on that date takes the purchase out of the policy) and whose plan name equals the plan bought, so every plan parameter read is the bought plan's (round-1 F-ANCHOR closed by scope).

4. Problem-tree card. Root -> maintenance_ext_retail_cancel_refund, value_input, gate trade_credit, form state, sentence above ("only after"; record-visible state; no code token; exact scope Essentials/Plus/Premium + sold or traded; only the retail cancellation policy books it). False at opening: initial_state.maintenance_plans.<plan_rav4>.status = active; initial_state.maintenance_cancellation_requests.<req_rav4> vehicle_sold_or_traded, submitted. Flip: maintenance_visits_cancelled entry (vehicle_sold_or_traded, 2026-10-21) -> trade-cycle credit 0.00 -> 50.00. Deletion run: 319.50 instead of 269.50. Order: cancellation (step 13) then contract (step 15). user_scenario never mentions the RAV4, its plan, a cancellation or a refund. Tools validate nothing.

5. Factor cards (authoring scratch run with check_compute.build_env/eval_compute/substitute; `check_compute.py ... --task 1` recomputes them).
Retail cancellation refund 421.05 (whole baseline 214.20 = 664.05 - 3 x 124.95 - 75.00):
- retail_refund_basis (method): financed on the installment contract -> pro rata 664.05 x 5/8 = 415.03; baseline retail-value amount 289.20 gives 295.22. Shapes: financed -> price x unused/included; unfinanced past half term -> min(retail value, price x day share); else retail value (round-1 F-DUPTIER closed: the tiers are keyed on financing and term run, and the lesser-of tier differs from the retail value whenever few visits were used late in the term).
- trade_up_fee (parameter): a vehicle price charge (46880.00, 2026-10-05, deal KTD-26-31884) within 1 whole month -> fee 0.00; baseline 75.00 gives 346.05.
- bundle_recapture_rate (parameter): sold on a deal below list, 43 whole months -> rate 0.4 x 34.95 = 13.98; baseline 0 gives 435.03.
- rewards_refund (parameter): Kessler Owner Rewards Gold -> 20.00; baseline gives 401.05.
415.03 - 0.00 - 13.98 + 20.00 = 421.05.
Retail plan price 269.50 (whole baseline 699.00):
- retail_basis (method): the Highlander's ToyotaCare (24 months / 25000 miles from 2026-10-07) -> months share (48 - 23)/48 = 0.520833, miles share (45000 - (25000 - 9))/45000 = 0.444644 -> 699.00 x 0.520833 = 364.0625; baseline list gives 591.04 (round-1 F-MLABEL closed: the tier now takes record inputs).
- owner_rewards (parameter): Gold -> 0.04; baseline 284.06.
- new_owner_enrollment (parameter): delivered 14 days -> 30.00; baseline 299.50 (round-1 F-WINDOW closed: a dollar allowance, monotone for every plan name).
- trade_cycle (parameter, multi-source): the replaced plan's sold-or-traded cancellation entry today (ledger) AND the replaced plan was sold on Kessler deal KTD-23-30962 (purchase record) -> 50.00; a replaced plan bought on its own would earn 25.00; no entry 0.00; every tier reachable inside the scope; baseline 319.50.
364.0625 x 0.96 = 349.50; less 80.00 = 269.50.

6. Base-invariant card. Cancellation: active_to_cancel, signed_request hold; request processed on its request date (in scope); no free look (sold 2023-03-18); no unwound deal (KTD-23-30962 closed). Sale: one_plan_per_vehicle (no plan on the Highlander); Plus 8-Visit eligible (new, 2026, odometer 1118 <= 36000, standalone allowed); single deal in delivered status (in scope). temporal_feasibility [].

7. Business-object card. KC-305118 + req_rav4; the new plan on the Highlander. Excluded: the closed RAV4 deal for the delivered-deal reads. Plan ledger: loaded 8 (2023-03-18), redemptions 2025-05-12 (24610), 2025-11-17 (30180), 2026-05-26 (35940) — after the RAV4's ToyotaCare ended 2025-03-18.

8. World rows. Customer, store KTD, RAV4 (no owner) and Highlander, Gold account SA-372915, deals KTD-23-30962 (closed) and KTD-26-31884 (delivered 2026-10-07, no trade-in, financed 41771.00 awaiting funding) with its ledger (deposit 1000.00 card 2026-10-01; vehicle price 46880.00, documentary fee 299.00 (KTD fee below the 10 percent ceiling), filing 24.00, sales tax 7.5 percent 3516.00, title/registration 52.00; deposit applied 2026-10-07; down payment 8000.00 check; balance 41771.00), ToyotaCare coverage on the Highlander, plan KC-305118 with its ledger and the request.

9. Persona. Celeste: volunteers only the goal; identity on request (name, phone 9375553271, license last four 3592, ZIP 45459); odometer 1118 on request; consents when told something must be taken care of; signs the contract herself; ends on confirmation.

10. Standard solution. Locate, verify, read plans, ledger, requests, vehicles (customer + RAV4), service account, deals, deal transactions, warranty coverages, stores; cancel KC-305118 at 421.05; hand over the contract: Highlander, Kessler Toyota of Dayton, Kessler Care Plus 8-Visit, odometer 1118, expiration 2030-10-21, expiration odometer 46118, price 269.50.

11. Revision log (round 2): retail price 472.39 -> 269.50 (basis proration, enrollment allowance replaces the delivery-window rate); refund unchanged at 421.05 with re-keyed method and fee tiers; Highlander deal carries no trade-in and its ledger is seeded for the fee read.


12. Revision log (round 3): F-UNREACH closed — the trade-cycle credit's second condition is now how the replaced plan was bought (sold on a Kessler deal: 50.00 / bought on its own: 25.00), reachable inside the scope, so the factor stays multi-source; F-FIRST closed — the replaced plan is defined by the most recent signed sold-or-traded request with a same-date tie rule; rounding stated half up to the cent in rule, docstring and tool body (half-up helper). Gold unchanged: 421.05, 269.50.

13. Revision log (round 4): F-HALFUP closed — every money RND is RND(x + 0.000000001, 2); tie probe (4 visits used: 664.05 x 4/8 = 332.025) gives 332.03 and a refund of 338.05 as the rule states; gold unchanged (421.05, 269.50).

Revision log (round 5): F-EPS closed per the coordinator rounding ruling — every money RND is RND(x + 0.000000001, 2) (epsilon 1e-9), so exact half-cent ties round up and no non-tie within 1e-6 of a half cent is pushed up; every rounded argument behind the scored, baseline and factor-sensitivity figures of this task sits at least 0.0013 from a half cent (checked by replaying gold). Gold unchanged.

Revision log (round 6, render scan F1): the retail plan price is floored at 0.00 after the credits and before rounding; the retail refund's overwrite restates the base refund for a request processed on a later day. Gold unchanged (421.05, 269.50).

Revision log (round 7, seed-only): S-1a — KTD-23-30962 hold_expires_date corrected to 2023-03-16 (reserved 2023-03-11 + 5-day New Vehicle Retail hold, day 0 = reservation date, no extension); no computation reads it. Gold unchanged (421.05, 269.50).
user_scenario:
You are Celeste Marchetti, a middle-school science teacher in Centerville, Ohio. You are calling on your lunch break, so you are warm but a little hurried, you speak in full sentences, and you appreciate it when someone explains a price in plain words.

Two weeks ago, on October 7th, you drove home a brand-new 2026 Toyota Highlander from Kessler Toyota of Dayton. You did not add a maintenance plan when you signed for the car, and now you have decided you want one: you are calling to buy the Kessler Care Plus 8-Visit plan for the Highlander today and to find out what it costs. That plan is your choice and you are not interested in comparing other plans; you have no other request.

You only give identifying details when the agent asks, a piece at a time: your name is Celeste Marchetti; your phone number on file is 9375553271; the last four characters of your driver's license are 3592; your home ZIP code is 45459. If you are asked for the date you first opened your profile, you say you honestly don't remember and offer another detail instead. If the agent asks for the Highlander's current mileage, you check the photo you took of the dashboard this morning: it reads 1118 miles. If the agent asks where or when you bought it, you repeat Kessler Toyota of Dayton, October 7th. You don't know any internal reference numbers and you are happy for the agent to look things up.

If the agent tells you that something on your account needs to be taken care of or booked before the plan can be priced or written, you listen and say that is fine, please go ahead; you do not raise anything of your own. If the agent asks whether they may handle items on your account for you, you say yes.

When the agent tells you the price of the Plus 8-Visit plan for the Highlander, you accept it. When the agent hands you the plan contract to sign, you sign it yourself with exactly the details the agent gives you and your own mileage reading. If the agent mentions a figure and later corrects it, you ask which one is final and go with that. Once the agent confirms the plan is signed and active on the Highlander, you thank them and say goodbye.
